speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) whether the Government will be checking the structural integrity of all oil pipelines in Singapore's waters; (b) what other measures can be taken to prevent the occurrence of future oil spills in Singapore's waters; and (c) whether any penalties will be imposed on the company responsible for the oil leak on 20 October 2024.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: It is an offence under the Environmental Protection and Management Act for any person to discharge any polluting matter into a watercourse.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: It is also an offence under the Prevention of Pollution of the Sea Act, to discharge any oil or oily mixture into Singapore waters from any place on land or from any apparatus used for transferring oil from or to any ship.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Industrial facilities typically conduct regular maintenance and inspections of equipment, including oil pipelines, to reduce the risk of leaks or failure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: NEA also conducts regular inspections of facilities with oil pipelines, such as refineries and petrochemical plants, to ensure compliance with environmental pollution standards' control requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: After it has conducted its investigations, NEA will share relevant learning points with other industrial facilities to review and strengthen their measures and standard operating procedures and to perform checks on their systems, where needed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: On the other measures to minimise the risk of oil spills, the Member may refer to the earlier response by the Minister of State for Transport, Mr Murali Pillai, to Parliamentary Questions on the recent oil spill incidents.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: She mentioned that there are regular inspections of the equipment.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Can I clarify, what frequency that would be?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Will this plan now be extended to cover the recent oil spills in October?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: First, let me say, as I have noted earlier in my response, the industrial facilities will typically conduct regular maintenance and inspections of their equipment, including the pipelines, to ensure there are no leaks or failures.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, the onus is actually on them to conduct this regular maintenance and checks on their equipment.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But NEA also conducts regular checks on these facilities with the oil pipelines, including petrochemical plants and refineries, to ensure that they comply with environmental pollution control requirements to make sure that the measures that they put in place for pollution control is effective.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Generally, we will check at the run-off of the discharge points, because if there is oil leak in any facility, the run-off will be contaminated.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We do it regularly, through the course of the year.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It may depend on the assessment by the agency as to how often they will need to do checks on these facilities.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I understand that they will continue to monitor this.
